Iran’s supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, was killed on the first day of strikes, and the strait of Hormuz – a crucial waterway for transporting oil – was effectively closed soon after. The conflict quickly became a regional war with global economic consequences.

# Live Updates: Iran war hits 6-month mark with no end in sight

Updated on: August 28, 2026 / 8:54 AM EDT
/ CBS News

## What to know about the Iran war today:

## Russia and Iran made "very good progress" in gas transfer talks, ambassador says

Russia and Iran made "very good progress" in talks held this week about transferring Russian gas to Iran via an overland pipeline through Azerbaijan, Iran's ambassador to Russia, Kazem Jalali, told IRNA, Iran's state-owned official news outlet.

The two sides — Iran's Ministry of Petroleum and Russia's state-owned Gazprom energy company — agreed to transfer an initial capacity of 150 million cubic meters per day through the pipeline, Jalali said.

The total would be equivalent to just shy of 1 million barrels per day. For comparison sake, about 21 million barrels of oil traveled through the Strait of Hormuz on a daily basis prior to the war, according to [the U.S. Energy Information Administration](https://www.eia.gov/international/analysis/special-topics/world_oil_transit_Chokepoints).

"We have reached an understanding on all these issues. Therefore, we are no longer at the initial stages of this project; rather, we have made very good progress," Jalali told IRNA. He said "one or two" issues remained to be ironed out.

Iran has consistently pursued different ways of acquiring oil and gas since the U.S. implemented a blockade on all traffic through the Strait of Hormuz entering or exiting Iranian ports.

The Economic Shock Waves of the War

By the second half of 2025, the Russia-Ukraine war has ceased to be merely a military conflict and has turned into a multi layered crisis that shakes the fundamental dynamics of the global economy. Beyond the conventional clashes on the front line, attacks on energy infrastructure, the targeting of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, comprehensive sanctions imposed on Russia and disruptions in supply chains have carried the economic cost of the war to a global scale.

These economic shock waves have not only been a problem faced by Western economies but have also been felt in different ways in countries such as Russia and China, which are either targets of sanctions or refuse to participate in them. According to reports from the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, the country’s economy has undergone significant structural transformations in the process of adapting to sanctions; import substitution policies and the shift towards Asian markets have accelerated (Central Bank of Russia, 2025).  Oliver Griffin is a policy and tech reporter at The Economy, focusing on the intersection of artificial intelligence, government regulation, and macroeconomic strategy. Prior to joining The Economy, he covered technology policy for an international think tank, producing research cited by major institutions, including the OECD and IMF. # [Grains Rally on Supply Fears, but Seaborne Flows Are Losing Steam](/insights/2026/8/28/grains-rally-on-supply-fears-but-seaborne-flows-are-losing-steam)

[Ocean Analytics](/insights?author=5f5eb5f2a3738d07d51ec64c)

*By* [*Ulf Bergman*](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ulf-bergman-81570425/)

Over the past two and a half weeks, grain and oilseed prices have soared. This follows a few months of volatility across the agricultural commodities market. Renewed concerns over supplies, amid an escalation of hostilities between Ukraine and Russia that is affecting exports from the Black Sea region, have contributed to gains in wheat prices over the past few weeks. At the same time, concerns over US crop yields have supported corn prices. In contrast, demand has been the primary driver for soybeans. The recent gains have propelled wheat and corn futures to their highest levels in just over three years, while soybean contracts are trading at levels last seen in May 2024.

The September futures for grains and oilseeds listed on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) have recorded significant gains over the last two and a half weeks. The September soybean futures have gained around eight per cent since the eleventh, while the wheat and corn contracts have surged by around fifteen per cent over the period.

Mighty and mysterious, the Black Sea is Ukraine’s treasure. Life on the coastline feels like a blessing – yet at the same time as a threat during wartime.

Russia is increasingly provoking escalation in the Black Sea region, attacking civilian cargo ships and port infrastructure. In gross violation of international law, the aggressor state threatens global food security. Daily shelling of the Odesa region blocks the crucial grain corridor, while also damaging marine ecosystems and leading to significant human losses.

Russia’s actions are a threat not only to Ukraine, but to the security of the entire Black Sea region. Protecting people and civilian shipping from Russian threats is therefore a shared challenge – one that requires Ukraine and its partners to stand together against Russia’s attempts to make the sea more dangerous.

# At least 1,924 people missing in Nepal after floods

![At least 1,924 people missing in Nepal after floods](https://cdn-cabinet.ua.news/uploads/images/nepal_floods_1924_people_missing_1787936088348.webp?7790911 "At least 1,924 people missing in Nepal after floods")

At least 1,924 people are considered missing after floods in Nepal. Search and rescue operations are continuing in Nepal and Tibet. Rescuers in Nepal are hindered by difficult Himalayan terrain, mud and the risk of further flooding.

## Data on missing people in Nepal

According to [ABC News Australia](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-08-29/death-toll-rises-as-rescuers-work-through-flood-devastation/107092742), Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reported that 517 foreign tourists are among those missing. Another 933 missing people were workers on hydropower projects on rivers.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel [Telegram](https://telegram.me/uanewsstream).

Nepal Army personnel continued search and rescue operations overnight. Those being searched for in Nepal include at least 38 Australian citizens.
